title: Keep preflight, chat input normalization, and Skill parser grammar aligned
goal: Ensure every documented create-file command variant accepted by chat preflight is passed intact to the Skill parser, including English polite lead-ins and alternate create/write phrasing.
context: A source audit after PACHAT-531 found that preflight and parseCreateFileRequest accept more variants than SkillRuntime.chatInputText preserves. Additionally, the Skill selector did not normalize English write/make verbs to the canonical create intent, so accepted variants could lose content or fail selection.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken workspace path allowlists, policy/approval gates, protected-path checks, size limits, or read-back verification.
Do not treat provider prose as proof of tool execution.
Do not modify release workflows or Alpha/Stable release configuration.
Do not claim physical-device verification without testing on a real iPhone.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight and chatInputText normalize the same documented Vietnamese/English polite prefixes before matching create-file grammar.
All supported create-file command variants preserve the full path and content boundary into Skill input.
English create/write/make variants select the canonical workspace.create-file Skill and execute verified writes with exact read-back content.
Current user request extraction continues to ignore earlier conversation turns.
Regression tests cover English and Vietnamese variants, content preservation, and complete preflight acceptance.
All changes stay within allowed_paths and required CI checks pass.
verification: Inspect Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA workflow results.
Physical iPhone acceptance remains tracked separately under Issue #347.
recovery: If grammar changes cause ambiguity, narrow the accepted variants and clarify unsupported requests; do not route malformed inputs to a write capability.
